the two species of the genus Philometra are parasitic in the body cavity of marine perciform fishes, and the new species is the only philometrid known to be parasitic in the tissues of marine perciforms, and the first species of the genus to be parasitic outside the body cavity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genus Philometroides can be distinguished from Philometra by the presence of a cephalic end with a pair of large papillae, and from other genera by the presence of two lateral pairs of small papillae of the internal circle and the absence of cephalic glands.
